title: Deep learning maps six high-potential deep-Earth scattering zones
summary: Researchers used deep learning with iterative manual optimization to identify 174,929 PKP precursors in more than two million earthquake waveforms recorded from 1990 to 2024. The expanded global map connected previously isolated sampling regions and highlighted six high-potential scattering zones near the core–mantle boundary that the authors report had not previously been documented. These are model-inferred targets for later seismic imaging, not fully characterized structures.
ai_technology: Deep-learning PKP precursor detector with human iterative optimization
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Researchers used deep learning with iterative manual optimization to identify 174,929 PKP precursors in more than two million earthquake waveforms recorded from 1990 to 2024.
evidence.unknown: The six features are high-potential scattering zones inferred from probability maps and proposed as targets for future multi-phase inversions; they are not precise outlines or independently characterized structures. The proposed thermochemical explanations are interpretations. Cross-validation with independent seismic phases supports multiple mapped ULVZs, but does not individually validate all six newly highlighted zones.
evidence.ai_role: The deep-learning detector screened over two million earthquake waveforms to identify 174,929 weak PKP precursor signals; researchers iteratively optimized detections manually. This AI-enabled catalog increased global sampling density by an order of magnitude and supported the dual-probability map that identified six previously undocumented high-potential scattering zones.
